newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Triple P in NLG 49 mln private placement.
newsitem.headline: Triple P in NLG 49 mln private placement.

text.p: Dutch software and services group Triple P NV said on Friday that it would raise about 49 million guilders through a private placement of shares.
The shares will be taken up by a group which includes existing shareholders, management, employees and institutional investors, the NASDAQ-listed company said.

It said it would issue 6.38 million new shares at $2 each, raising about 25 million guilders, plus 24 million nine percent cumulative preferential shares for 24 million guilders. The entire issue of preferential stock would be taken up by a single Dutch institutional investor, Triple P said without elaborating.
The two largest subscribers to the issue of new common shares would be investment fund Orange Fund NV and unlisted venture capital group Paribas Deelnemingen.

Triple P said its founder and current president Fezi Khaleghi Yazdi would transfer at no cost about 2.55 million of his Triple P shares on a pro-rata basis to the investors' group and 0.25 million shares to the employee stock option plan.
This would cut Khaleghi Yazdi's stake in the company to 26 percent from 44. Triple P said in June that Khaleghi Yazdi would resign as CEO on September 1 of this year.
The stake of other current shareholders would fall to 44 percent from 55 percent and the management's and employees' interest would rise to six percent from one percent.
The new investors taking up the common and preferential shares would hold a 24 percent stake in Triple P after the completion of the refinancing arrangement.

Triple P said the proceeds of the share placement would be used to restructure the firm's operations, which would require a substantially higher provision than the five to 10 million guilders which was expected earlier. The proceeds would also be used for repayment of debts and general working capital.
Triple P said the refinancing package would significantly strengthen its balance sheet and enable the company to restructure and reposition itself.
The refinancing is subject to approval by shareholders, who will meet on July 30.
Triple P said in May it had suffered a net loss of 4.9 million guilders in the first quarter of 1997, compared with a profit of 2.7 million in the same period of 1996.
